item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports adapting recurrent state updates to distinguish stable preferences from changing intent. [TIEN (2024)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S095741742301905X) incorporates time intervals, item information, hidden states and reset gates into an attention-modified GRU for interest evolution. [FAAM-SR (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0020025526005116) describes a frequency-enhanced GRU that adaptively balances frequent behaviors and exploratory interests. These provide architectural motivation, but neither establishes gains under the pinned RecHarness evaluation.\n\nDirect time-gated GRU precedents predate the requested window. [Sequential Recommender via Time-aware Attentive Memory Network (2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) uses a time-aware GRU for short-term intent alongside historical memory; [ACA-GRU (2020)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0020025519308539) modifies update/reset gates using contextual information. A compatible experimental hypothesis is therefore one jointly trained GRU4Rec network whose retention/reset gates depend on the current item, previous state and observed log-scaled time gap. Preserve some state dimensions for persistent interests while allowing others to reset rapidly. This is an inference from the literature, not a verified improvement: compare against the corrected baseline using macro validation HR@10, mask padding updates, read the final nonpadding state, and use only timestamps available consistently during training and prediction."}
